A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SafeOR-Gym and the same nine core environment families. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renamed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original training curves, evaluation rewards and costs, constraint-violation analyses, and runtimes for five safe RL algorithms.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of further RL algorithms, stochastic maintenance, and classical inventory policies.

M1.justification: The benchmark gains a localized environment-model extension: SchedMaintEnv-v1 uniformly samples compressor failure times from MTTF, MTTF−1, and MTTF−2 at episode initialization (Appendix A.8). The deterministic version remains, and no new learning algorithm is proposed.

E1.justification: The nine task families remain. Evaluation adds stochastic compressor failures through SchedMaintEnv-v1 and removes the GTEP scenario without transmission lines. Standard GTEP, multi-bus unit commitment, and ASU evaluations are retained despite changes in placement.

E2.justification: FOCOPS, SACLag, and SACPID join the original five algorithms in the retained comparisons. Appendix C.3 also evaluates classical (s, S) and (r, Q) inventory policies against the RL reward results, substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 replaces v1's cost-filtered best/worst selection with Pareto identification and normalized scalarization over 101 preference weights. It specifies a cost threshold of 25 for reasonable optimality and introduces a perfect-information optimization upper bound for stochastic maintenance. Evaluation remains based on 10 episodes.

E4.justification: v2 adds reward–safety preference sensitivity analyses in Figures 3 and 13 and compares deterministic versus stochastic maintenance behavior. Constraint-wise diagnostics expand to eight algorithms. Conversely, v1's blending disable/none ablations and generation-expansion analysis without transmission are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions describe standard-deviation bands for training curves. Unlike v1's mean-only evaluation tables, v2 Table 4 explicitly reports standard deviations for selected stochastic-maintenance results. The 10-episode evaluation count is unchanged; additional independent training runs are not established.

E6.justification: The original algorithms' retained deterministic evaluation values are unchanged, but substantial results are added for three algorithms, stochastic maintenance, and inventory heuristics. New SACLag results on GridStorageEnv are reward −68690.5 and cost 0.03, supporting its revised solvability classification. The (r, Q) policy obtains reward 10948.9 versus OnCRPO's retained 7598.66. Results for the removed variants disappear.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a formal normalized scalarized score for Pareto comparisons and a stochastic failure-time assumption. Appendix A also revises state-set definitions, including equipment in STN and restricting observed inventory to main supply-chain nodes. Most environmental equations remain equivalent, and no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: nine OR environments, Gym/OmniSafe integration, and empirical diagnosis of safe RL limitations under complex constraints. v2 explicitly calls the work a benchmarking and diagnostic study, clarifying rather than changing its original contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the brief overall discussion with extensive interpretations by algorithm class, linking behavior to trust-region updates, replay-based estimation, and discontinuous constraint landscapes. It adds qualifications about scalarization favoring high-violation policies and deterministic coverage. ASU is now interpreted as failing feasibility despite reasonably competitive rewards.

D1.justification: New Section 4 documents the small CMDP wrapper, external JSON instance specifications, and extension through inheritance. Further details include stochastic failure sampling, inventory-policy trigger bounds, and runtimes for added methods and scenarios. The repository access information and hardware remain the same.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SAC, PID constraint control, FOCOPS, and Powell's sequential-decision framework. Table 1 and Appendix D expand comparisons with OR-Gym and SustainGym, including interfaces and observation/action dimensions. The central positioning around industrial constraints beyond existing benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The environment overview is reorganized to cover all nine families, a dedicated implementation section is introduced, and the results discussion is extensively rewritten around multi-objective evaluation and algorithm classes. Evaluation tables and supplementary discussions are reorganized into separate appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adds eight environment schematics, evaluation bar charts, Pareto-score plots, and comparison and summary tables. Earlier evaluation tables are consolidated into a rotated appendix table, existing plots expand to eight algorithms, and several variant plots are removed. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the benchmark's evidential value through broader algorithm comparisons, an evaluated stochastic scenario, and classical inventory reward references that challenge the learned policies. Explicit reward–safety analysis and implementation documentation address important evaluation and usability gaps. Removing blending and topology ablations reduces diagnostic coverage, scalarized winners can remain highly infeasible, and classical-policy costs are unreported. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains.
